original_title: DraftLoop: Self-Speculative Decoding with Early-Exit Draft Heads for Lossless LLM Inference Acceleration
body: Autoregressive decoding in large language models (LLMs) is memory-bandwidth bound: each generated token requires a full forward pass through all layers. Speculative decoding mitigates this by letting a small draft model propose several tokens that the large target model verifies in parallel, but it requires training and serving a separate draft model. We propose DraftLoop, a self-speculative decoding method that attaches lightweight early-exit draft heads to intermediate layers of the target model itself, so no external draft model is needed. Draft heads are trained for 6 GPU-hours with the target model frozen. On Llama-3-70B, DraftLoop achieves a 2.4x wall-clock speedup over standard autoregressive decoding and 1.3x over Medusa, while provably preserving the target model's output distribution (lossless). Quality on MT-Bench is unchanged. Memory overhead is 1.8% of model parameters. Limitations: speedup decreases as batch size grows and falls below 1.2x at batch size 32, and we evaluate only English benchmarks. Code and draft-head weights are released under the Apache-2.0 license.
